content:
Let \(P(x)\) be the product of the digits of \(x\). We need
\[
P(x)=x^2-10x-22.
\]
Since \(P(x)\ge 0\), we need \(x^2-10x-22\ge 0\), so \(x\ge 12\).

If \(x\) has at least 3 digits, then \(x\ge 100\), so
\[
x^2-10x-22 \ge 10000-1000-22=8978,
\]
but for a 3-digit number \(P(x)\le 9^3=729\), and more generally \(P(x)\le 9^n\). Thus \(x\) must have at most 2 digits. Since \(x\ge 12\), \(x\) is two-digit.

Let \(x=10a+b\), with \(1\le a\le 9\), \(0\le b\le 9\). Then
\[
ab=(10a+b)^2-10(10a+b)-22.
\]
Expanding and simplifying gives
\[
b^2+(19a-10)b+100a^2-100a-22=0.
\]
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(19a-10)^2-4(100a^2-100a-22)=-39a^2+20a+188.
\]
Since \(\Delta\ge 0\), testing \(a=1,2,\dots\) gives only \(a=1\) possible, with
\[
\Delta=169=13^2.
\]
Then
\[
b^2+9b-22=0,
\]
so \(b=2\) or \(b=-11\). Thus \(b=2\), and
\[
x=12.
\]

Check: \(P(12)=1\cdot 2=2\), and
\[
12^2-10\cdot 12-22=144-120-22=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
